meta.title: Tavvit: group chat with channels, voice and screen sharing
meta.description: Tavvit is a home for your friends and communities: channels, direct messages, voice and screen sharing in one quick, quiet app. No ads, no trackers.

hero.title: Where your group talks.
hero.lead: Channels, direct messages, voice and screen sharing for your friends and communities, in one quick, quiet app. No ads, no trackers.
hero.alt: The Tavvit app: a space's channels on the left, a conversation in the middle and its members on the right.

spaces.title: Spaces
spaces.body: The places you are in, as named tabs.

channels.title: Channels
channels.body: A space's channels, sorted into categories.

conversation.title: The conversation
conversation.body: Code, replies that show what they answer, mentions and reactions.

members.title: Members
members.body: Everyone under their role, and who is online.

statement: Everything your group needs in one place, and nothing that follows you around. Quick to open, quiet to live in, and yours to shape.

figures.note: Every feature on this page is in the app, and every number is the app's own.

demo.label: A demo channel
demo.title:
Go on,
say something.
demo.body: This is what a channel feels like. Type a message and see who answers.
demo.note: A demo: the people are invented, and nothing you type leaves this page.

seed.lena: Always. I think someone new just walked in.
seed.noor: Hey, new here? Pull up a chair and say hi!

replies.lena: Welcome! Grab a seat, nobody bites.
replies.sam: Good timing. We need one more for tonight.
replies.noor: I like this one. Can we keep them?
replies.theo: Is that why I am always last?
replies.yuki: Noted. I will add you to the spreadsheet.
replies.end: You are getting the hang of this. The real thing has voice, threads and a lot more.

spaces.title: A space for every group.
spaces.body: The raid team, the book club, the people you build things with. Each gets its own space, with channels sorted into categories and a member list that shows who does what.
spaces.alt: A space's channel list next to its member list, grouped by coloured roles.

alts.raid: A gaming group's space: a conversation about one more round, with a code block and reactions.
alts.photo: A photo club's space: a channel where people give feedback on a roll of film.
alts.dev: A developer group's space: a code review channel with a message from a build bot.
alts.books: A book club's space: a conversation about this month's book.

messages.title:
Conversations
that stay readable.
messages.body: A channel you can read in the morning and still follow. Nothing jumps, nothing shouts, and a message that mentions you is easy to spot.
messages.alt: A conversation with replies, a code block, mentions and reactions.

replies.title: Replies show what they answer
replies.body: A reply carries a line of the message it answers, so you never scroll back to find out.

reactions.title: Reactions stay small
reactions.body: A row of small counts under a message, never a wall of them.

content.title: Code, links and files sit where they belong
content.body: A code block keeps its colours, a link shows a preview, and a file shows what it is.

switcher.title: Back to where you left off
switcher.body: Unread channels stand out, the inbox gathers what is waiting for you, and Ctrl+K takes you to any channel or conversation in a few keystrokes.

around.title: Everything around the conversation.
around.body: A group does more than talk. Side conversations, plans, votes and house rules sit right beside the chat.

thread.title: Threads
thread.body: Pull a side conversation out of the channel. Follow the ones you care about, and the rest stay out of your way.
thread.alt: A channel with a thread open beside it.

poll.title: Polls
poll.body: Ask the room. Results stay hidden until you have voted, so the first votes do not steer the rest.
poll.alt: A poll with three answers and the share of votes for each.

welcome.title: A welcome and rules
welcome.body: Greet new people, point them to the right channels and, if you like, ask them to agree to your rules first.
welcome.alt: A space's welcome with its rules and the channels to start in.

event.title: Events
event.body: Plan the raid or the book club, see who is going, get a reminder and add it to your calendar.
event.alt: An event with its date, who is going and a button to join the voice channel.

voice.title: Voice messages and a soundboard
voice.body: Say it instead of typing it, and play a sound to the whole voice channel when the moment calls for one.

saved.title: Saved messages and reminders
saved.body: Keep what matters in one list, and have a message brought back to you later.

alerts.title: Keyword alerts and push
alerts.body: Choose the words that should reach you, and get a notification even when the app is closed.

profiles.body: A banner, a bio, pronouns, links and colours of your choice, and if you like a different picture and bio for each space.
profiles.alt: A profile card with a banner, a bio and a role.

friends.title:
Your people,
one click away.
friends.body: Add friends by their username, see who is online and what they are up to, and start a direct message or a group of up to ten.
friends.alt: The friends page, listing who is online and what they are doing.

voice.title:
Talk when typing
is too slow.
voice.body: Drop into a voice channel, turn on your camera, share your screen or ring a friend directly. Noise suppression filters out your keyboard, and push to talk is one setting away.
voice.alt: A voice channel with several people in it and the call controls below.

screen.title: Screen sharing
screen.body: Show the game, the slides or the bug, at the quality you choose.

noise.title: Noise suppression
noise.body: Your keyboard, your fan and the street stay out of the call.

calls.title: Calls in direct messages
calls.body: Ring one person or a group, with video if you like.

items.themes: Seven themes, or your own colours
items.contrast: High contrast and clear status shapes
items.phone: On your phone, added to the home screen
items.template: Start from a Discord server template
items.botApi: REST and socket API for bots
items.push: Notifications when the app is closed

community.title:
Find a space,
or open your own.
community.body: Browse public spaces on Explore and join with one click or a request. A verified mark means the platform team has reviewed a space, and no space can list itself without that review.
community.alt: The Explore page with cards for public spaces.

explore.title: Listed after review
explore.body: A space appears on Explore only after the platform team has approved it.

moderation.title: Tools for moderators
moderation.body: Timeouts, slow mode, automatic moderation and an audit log of who did what.

reports.title: Reports that are answered
reports.body: Anyone can report a message or a space, and people affected are told the decision and the reason.

rights.title: Rights down to the channel
rights.body: Roles with their own colours and permissions, and exceptions for any category or channel.

invites.title: Invites on your terms
invites.body: Links with an end date and a limit, or join requests you approve one by one.

template.title: Start from a template
template.body: Paste a Discord server template and get its roles, categories, channels and permissions. Messages and members stay where they are.

moving.title: Opening your own takes three steps.

one.title: Set up your place
one.body: Start a new space, or bring your Discord server: its roles, categories and channels from a template, its emoji and stickers with a bot of your own.

two.title: Send one link
two.body: Everyone joins with the same invite link. Give it an end date or a limit if you like.

three.title: Pull up a chair
three.body: Your group is in. Channels and voice work right away, and the rest is yours to shape.

developers.title: Build on it.
developers.body: Bots post, react, moderate and answer slash commands through a documented API. Webhooks take a message from any program with a single address.
developers.alt: A message from a bot, marked as one, with a card showing how a build went.

api.title: A documented API
api.body: REST and a live socket, with a quickstart that gets a first bot talking in minutes.

commands.title: Slash commands
commands.body: With text, numbers, people, channels and fixed choices, and answers only the person who asked can see.

rights.title: Bots ask, you decide
rights.body: A bot gets only the rights a space gives it, and its mark cannot be turned off.

privacy.title:
No ads.
No trackers.
privacy.body: Pictures and videos from other websites load only after you click them, so those sites learn nothing about you until you decide.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.body: An authenticator app and recovery codes guard your account.

devices.title: Your devices in view
devices.body: See where you are signed in, and sign out one device or all of them.

data.title: Take it with you, or delete it
data.body: Download your data as one file, or delete your account yourself.

contact.title: You decide who reaches you
contact.body: Choose who may send you a friend request or start a conversation, and block anyone.

themes.title:
Your colours,
your density.
themes.body: Seven themes or your own colours, three message styles, sharp or round corners, and the text size you read best. Tavvit stays out of the way, in whichever look you like.
themes.alt: The same conversation in the {{name}} theme.

anywhere.title:
On your desktop.
On your phone.

desktop.body: A Windows app with global shortcuts, automatic updates and game detection, so friends can see what you are playing.

phone.body: Open Tavvit in your phone's browser and add it to the home screen. Spaces, messages and voice come along, and notifications reach you even when it is closed.
phone.alt: Tavvit on a phone, showing a conversation.

anywhere.qr: Scan to open Tavvit on your phone

join.q: How do I join a space?
join.a: Open an invite link from someone in it, or browse Explore for public spaces. Some spaces let you in at once, others ask for a request first.

phone.a: Tavvit runs in your phone's browser. Add it to the home screen and it opens like an app, with notifications. It is not in the app stores.

computers.q: Which computers does it run on?
computers.a: Any with a current browser. For Windows there is also a desktop app with global shortcuts, automatic updates and game detection.

moving.q: Can I bring my Discord server along?
moving.a: Its structure and its emoji, yes. Paste a server template link and Tavvit sets up the roles, categories, channels and permissions; with a bot of your own, the server's emoji and stickers come along too. Messages and members cannot, so invite your people with a link.

bots.a: Yes. Anyone can write one with the public API, and whoever runs a space decides which bots come in and what they may do. Start with the developer docs.

trouble.a: Moderators have timeouts, bans, automatic filters and an audit log. Anyone can report a message or a space, and people affected are told the decision and the reason.

cta.title: There's a seat free.
cta.body: Create an account in a minute and start your first space, or join one you were invited to.
cta.closed: This server is not taking new accounts at the moment. If you have one, welcome back.

closer: That's the whole page. Your chair's still free.
